notes: pr-dev is the final delivery lifecycle driver: once per objective, not once per worker. Eval 4 is the regression for spec defect 13 — auto-merge must never be forced against repository or user policy. Eval 5 covers loose-vs-strict branch updates and CI supersession. Evals 1-3 preserve the original drive-loop behaviour.

evals.prompt: Finish PR #42. Address any review comments and get it merged.
evals.expected_output: Resolves objective context and merge policy at startup, reports both in one or two lines, enables auto-merge because the repository allows it, then runs the persistent loop: fetch state, address threads, fix CI, re-apply policy after each push, poll until merged, run cleanup.
expectations: resolve-merge-policy.sh is run before the first loop pass
The resolved policy and its source are stated to the user
Auto-merge is enabled because the resolved policy says enable — not because it is hardcoded
Review threads are stated in conversation before replies are posted
The loop restarts immediately after any push rather than stopping
State is re-fetched before every merge-readiness decision
cleanup-after-merge.sh runs after the merge

evals.prompt: Drive PR #17 to merge. CI is currently failing.
evals.expected_output: Classifies each non-green check against the current head commit, patches branch-related failures, pushes, re-applies merge policy, and restarts. Flaky infra reruns are capped at 3 for the PR. Superseded/cancelled runs from older commits are ignored, not retried.
expectations: Only checks on the current headRefOid are graded
A cancelled run on a superseded commit is not treated as a failure and does not consume the flake budget
Branch-related failures are patched and pushed rather than retried
Infra flakes are rerun at most 3 times, then escalated
Failures in non-required checks are reported but do not block merge
CI config and tests are not edited to silence a failure

assertions.text: No more than 3 gh run rerun invocations occur
Superseded cancelled runs are explicitly excluded from the failure set

evals.prompt: Address the review on my PR and merge it when done.
evals.expected_output: Resolves the PR from the current branch, works through every unresolved thread (assess, state the reply, post, fix, resolve), reaches the readiness gate, and merges under the resolved policy. Does not require the user to type 'approved' when policy is auto-merge.
expectations: The PR number is inferred from the current branch
Each thread gets an explicit agree / partially agree / disagree assessment
resolve-thread.sh is used to resolve threads after replying
REVIEW_REQUIRED alone is not treated as blocked when auto-merge is enabled
The final report names the merge SHA, checks, fixes and branch deletion

evals.prompt: Drive PR #88 to merge. Note: this repo's objective sets delivery.auto_merge=false — I want to press the button myself.
evals.expected_output: Merge policy resolves to skip, sourced from the objective's delivery.auto_merge=false. The skill drives the PR to green and to zero unresolved threads, prints the readiness summary, and ASKS before merging. It never calls gh pr merge --auto.
expectations: resolve-merge-policy.sh reports auto_merge=skip with the objective as the source
No `gh pr merge --auto` call is made at any point
The skill still drives CI and threads to done
At the readiness gate the user is asked before any merge happens
The reason auto-merge was skipped is stated, not silently applied

assertions.text: The string `--auto` never appears in an executed gh pr merge command
The user is asked for merge confirmation at the readiness gate
The policy source (objective delivery.auto_merge=false) is reported

evals.prompt: PR #12 says it's 3 commits behind main and one check shows as cancelled. Get it merged.
evals.expected_output: Checks strict_branch_update from branch protection. On a loose base, the behind state is left alone rather than churned with base merges; on a strict base the branch is updated exactly once. The cancelled check is identified as a superseded run on an older commit and ignored.
expectations: strict_branch_update is read from the resolved policy rather than assumed
On a loose base, no base-merge or update-branch is performed
On a strict base, gh pr update-branch is run once, not in a loop
The cancelled check is diagnosed as supersession and not rerun
If a merge queue exists, the PR is enqueued and the branch is not further updated

assertions.text: gh pr update-branch is invoked at most once
No base branch merge is performed when strict_branch_update is false or null

evals.prompt: The objective auth-system has 5 finished tasks on worker branches. Ship it.
evals.expected_output: Recognises that delivery is one PR for the objective: it drives the single PR opened from the integration branch objective/auth-system. It does not open or drive a PR per worker branch, and it pushes fixes only to the integration branch.
expectations: The integration branch is identified from objective.json
Exactly one PR is driven
No PR is opened for any worker/* branch
Fixes are pushed to the integration branch, never to an already-merged worker branch
On merge, the objective status is set to completed and delivery.pr_url is recorded

assertions.text: No gh pr create call targets a worker/* branch
Exactly one PR number is driven throughout the run

evals.prompt: Drive PR #55 to merge on a platform with no background tasks.
evals.expected_output: Capability fallback case. The Monitor until-loop is unavailable, so the skill falls back to the documented foreground polling cadence. Everything else — thread handling, CI classification, policy-resolved merge — is unchanged, and the skill does not claim to be watching in the background.
expectations: background_tasks is treated as optional; its absence degrades to the polling cadence table
references/ci-monitor-loop.md is not required for the run to complete
The skill does not claim work is proceeding in the background when it is not
Polling still never stops on a single idle poll
Merge policy resolution and the review-thread loop are unaffected by the degradation
